FREE Cozy Fall Fingerless Gloves - Quick 1 Hour Make

These cozy chunky fingerless gloves are my favorite quick fall make — warm hands, free fingers for coffee cups and phone, and so cute with the thumb hole.

I made them in cream and rust super chunky yarn, perfect for chilly morning walks, pumpkin patch days, and coffee runs. One hour, 8mm hook, beginner-friendly rectangle with a thumb gap — no shaping needed.

Skill level Beginner - 1 hour quick
Hook 8 mm crochet hook
Yarn Super chunky / bulky

Before you begin

I've been living in fingerless gloves this fall — they keep my wrists and hands warm but I can still hold my coffee, scroll, and pick up pinecones on walks. This pair turned out exactly how I wanted — chunky but soft, not stiff.

What I love is it's just a rectangle. No fingers to shape. We crochet a rectangle where the chain edge is the length of the glove (wrist to below knuckles) and the rows grow the width that wraps around your hand. Fold it in half so the first and last rows meet, seam the side, leave a little gap for the thumb — that's it. One rectangle per glove.

If you can chain and half double crochet, you can make these. The thumb hole is just a skip — we leave about 1.5 inches (4 rows) open when we seam.

Tip from my table: My rectangle is 22 chains = 7 inches tall (wrist to knuckles) and 24 rows = 8 inches wide when flat. When seamed into a tube it becomes about 8 inches around relaxed, 9.5 inches stretched — perfect S/M. For smaller hands ch 20, for larger ch 24 for extra height, and adjust rows: 22 rows for smaller circumference, 26 for larger.

Materials I used

  • Super chunky yarn: About 80 yards total for pair — I used cream (40 yards) and rust (40 yards). One skein of each is plenty. Acrylic or wool blend both work lovely and cozy.
  • 8mm crochet hook: Keeps fabric soft and drapey, not tight.
  • Tapestry needle: For seaming sides and leaving thumb hole.
  • Scissors & stitch marker: To mark first stitch of each row.

Sizing & how to measure

This pattern is for size S/M — about 7 inches tall (wrist to below knuckles) and 8 inches around relaxed, stretches to 9.5 inches.

  • Measure: Around your hand at knuckles (circumference) and from wrist to just below knuckles (height).
  • My rectangle flat: Chain 22 = 7 inches tall, 24 rows = 8 inches wide. So flat size is 7" (tall) x 8" (wide). When you fold and seam the 8" wide side into a tube, the tube circumference is 8" — matches your hand measurement. The 7" stays as glove height.
  • Thumb hole: Leave 1.5 inches (4 rows) open in side seam — positioned about 2.5 inches up from bottom edge.
Orientation check: If you lay your rectangle flat, the chain edge and opposite edge are the top (fingers) and bottom (wrist). The two side edges (first row and last row) are what you seam together to make the tube around your hand.

Abbreviations

US terms:

  • ch - chain
  • hdc - half double crochet
  • sl st - slip stitch
  • st - stitch

Full roadmap - 4 steps

Whole cozy gloves at a glance:

Step 1: Chain 22 with 8mm hook
Step 2: Rows 1-24: hdc across — 4 rows rust, 4 rows cream repeat
Step 3: Fold rectangle, seam bottom 8 rows, leave 4 rows for thumb, seam top 12 rows (=24 total)
Step 4: Make second glove same, weave ends, shape thumb holes

Step-by-step with photos

1 Foundation chain

With cream or rust yarn and 8mm hook, ch 22. Keep it loose — this chain is the height of your glove, about 7 inches from wrist to below knuckles.

2 Body - rectangle with stripes

Row 1: hdc in 2nd ch from hook and across (21 hdc). Ch 1, turn.

Rows 2-24: hdc across (21 hdc each row). I did 4 rows cream, 4 rows rust, repeat — 24 rows total = 8 inches wide. This width will wrap around your hand to become the circumference. Stripe pattern gives that cozy fall look from your flatlay.

3 Fold & make thumb hole (math fixed: 8 + 4 + 12 = 24)

Fold rectangle so the first row and last row meet — you're bringing the two short sides together to form a tube around your hand. The chain edge is at top (fingers) and bottom is wrist. With tapestry needle and matching yarn:

  • Seam bottom 8 rows from wrist edge up (about 2.5 inches) — this is the wrist part.
  • Skip 4 rows — leave open — this is your thumb hole (about 1.5 inches).
  • Seam top 12 rows from thumb hole to finger edge (about 3.5 inches) — this closes the top of the hand.

8 + 4 + 12 = 24 rows — now fully seamed with only the thumb gap open. No missing rows.

4 Second glove & finish

Make second rectangle exactly same. Weave all ends with tapestry needle. Try on, poke thumb through hole, shape with fingers.

How I finish mine

I weave ends going around thumb hole once to reinforce it so it doesn't stretch. For photos, I place them on rustic wood with pinecones, dried orange slices, acorns and eucalyptus — little fall morning from my table, just like your flatlay inspiration.

Ways to make it your own

  • Color play: Oatmeal + rust, cream + mustard, solid cream, or pumpkin + chocolate — all cozy fall.
  • Mug cozy set: Use leftover yarn to make matching mug cozy — same rectangle but smaller, 20 sts x 12 rows, seam without thumb hole.
  • Longer version: Add 6 more rows for wrist warmers that go up arm — great for under coat.
  • Matching ear warmer: Pair with your twisted ear warmer in same yarn — perfect gift set.

Troubleshooting

  • Thumb hole too tight? Skip 5 rows instead of 4 — gives extra 0.5 inch. Super chunky yarn is thick, so 4 rows is usually perfect but hands vary.
  • Glove feels too narrow? Add 2 more rows (26 total) — remember rows = circumference. Then seam as 8 + 4 + 14 = 26.
  • Glove feels too short/long? Chain 20 for shorter (6.5") or 24 for longer (8") — chain = height.
  • Gap at top not closing? Check you seamed 12 rows at top, not 6. 8+4+6 was a typo — now fixed to 8+4+12 = 24.
  • Seam showing? Seam on wrong side with whip stitch, then turn right-side out. Use same color yarn as stripe you're seaming.

Caring for your gloves

Hand wash gently in cool water, lay flat to dry. Acrylic is forgiving. Shape thumb holes with fingers after washing. Reinforce thumb hole with an extra stitch around opening if it stretches.
